name: Stonepeak Partners LP

ownership.notes: Delaware limited partnership; SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD 159699, SEC 801-73350) since 6 March 2012. Michael Dorrell controls the adviser through its general partner, Stonepeak Partners LLC. Blue Owl's GP Strategic Capital funds have held a minority interest in Stonepeak Partners Holdings LP since June 2023; third-party owners receive less than 17% of fee income and carried interest and have no control (Form ADV).

summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Stonepeak signs for no equipment itself. It reaches this corpus through data-centre and storage platforms it controls or created. Cologix, recapitalised at a USD 3.0bn equity value in 2022, runs 45-plus interconnection data centres and is AEP Ohio's customer for onsite fuel-cell power. Digital Edge reports 1.8 GW of secured IT power across Asia. Montera, launched in April 2025 on a USD 1.5bn Stonepeak commitment, is building a 500 MW campus in Arizona. Kingdom owns nine Japanese battery projects (479 MW), and its first project financing names CATL batteries. Its biggest power positions are non-controlling. It holds 50% of Dominion's 2.6 GW Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project, where Dominion keeps full operational control, and 40% of Woodside's Louisiana LNG. Two signed deals would add controlled buyers on closing: a majority of the Louisiana utility Cleco (2,676 MW of generation, with Bernhard Capital) and a majority of Castrol (about USD 10.1bn enterprise value).

**BACKGROUND.** Per its Form ADV (filed 7 April 2026), the adviser is Stonepeak Partners LP, a Delaware limited partnership controlled by co-founder and chief executive Michael Dorrell through its general partner. It reports USD 81.9bn of regulatory assets under management across 125 accounts and 359 employees. Stonepeak's own published AUM is about USD 93bn as of March 2026, including subsequently committed capital. Blue Owl's GP Strategic Capital funds have held a minority interest since June 2023, with no control. The manager files no financial statements; its wealth fund, Stonepeak-Plus Infrastructure Fund, files 10-Ks. Infrastructure Investor's 2026 ranking places Stonepeak sixth in five-year infrastructure fundraising, at USD 52.9bn.
ecosystemRole: We assess Stonepeak as the capital segment's platform builder. Rather than buying established operators, it launches companies around management teams and funds their growth: Digital Edge (2020), the Japanese battery platform now called Kingdom (2024), Montera (2025) and WahajPeak (2025). It also controls Cologix through a dedicated continuation vehicle. Each of those platforms buys its own power and electrical equipment, and its own management signs. Cologix's president's remit includes data-centre design, engineering, construction and supply chain. Kingdom's first financing names CATL batteries, and Montera's delivery team comes from Oracle and Equinix. Its largest power cheques sit beside an operator — Dominion at CVOW, Woodside at Louisiana LNG, Repsol and Ørsted in US renewables — so there a seller's counterparty is the operator, not Stonepeak.

productsAndServices.name: Infrastructure funds — the flagship closed-end series
productsAndServices.description: Stonepeak's core product is a series of closed-end infrastructure funds that buy controlling or significant positions in digital, energy, transport and logistics, and real-estate businesses. Per the funds' Form D filings, Stonepeak Infrastructure Fund IV sold its full USD 14.0bn offering to 373 investors (final amendment, February 2022), and Fund V had sold USD 7.29bn with the offering marked 'Indefinite' at its latest amendment (January 2025); no final close for Fund V is on the record. The adviser reported USD 81.9bn of regulatory assets under management across 125 accounts, 121 of them pooled vehicles, in its Form ADV filed 7 April 2026.
highlights: Fund III's gross asset value was about USD 9.0bn and Fund IV's about USD 12.7bn across its main and Luxembourg vehicles, per the ADV's private-fund schedule, which excludes uncalled commitments

Single-asset vehicles sit beside the funds: Stonepeak Cologix Holdings LP carried about USD 5.0bn of gross asset value, the result of the 2022 recapitalisation that moved Cologix from Fund II into Stonepeak-managed vehicles
Infrastructure Investor's 2026 five-year fundraising table (published 1 June 2026, as carried in this corpus) lists Stonepeak ahead of Blackstone, behind BlackRock, KKR, Brookfield, Macquarie and EQT
productsAndServices.positioning: A specialist infrastructure manager, not a diversified alternative-asset firm: it has no buyout, hedge-fund or insurance arm, and its regulatory AUM is about a twelfth of Apollo's total AUM.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Closed-end limited partnerships with Luxembourg parallels, single-asset continuation vehicles and co-investment vehicles; 38% of clients are non-US persons (Form ADV).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Fund V's final close is not on the record; Stonepeak Asia Infrastructure Fund II and Global Renewables Fund II were still selling interests at their latest Form D amendments (July and April 2026).

productsAndServices.name: Digital infrastructure platforms — Cologix, Digital Edge and Montera
productsAndServices.description: Stonepeak controls three data-centre operators that buy their own power and electrical equipment. Cologix, bought in 2017 and recapitalised in 2022 at a USD 3.0bn equity value, runs '45+ hyperscale edge data centers across 13 North American markets' (Cologix, March 2026); Stonepeak is its controlling shareholder through Stonepeak Cologix Holdings, a single-asset vehicle with about USD 5.0bn of gross asset value in the Form ADV. Digital Edge was formed with Stonepeak in August 2020 on a USD 1bn capital commitment and reported 31 data centres and 1.8 GW of secured IT power across Asia in its April 2026 sustainability report. Montera Infrastructure, launched in April 2025 on a USD 1.5bn Stonepeak equity commitment, develops hyperscale campuses in North America; its one published project is PHX1 in Glendale, Arizona (500 MW, in service in the second quarter of 2028).
highlights: Cologix: a USD 1.5bn raise in October 2024 (a USD 1.0bn development debt facility plus USD 500m of equity) for over 650 critical MW of sellable capacity in Columbus, Des Moines and Vancouver; a 154-acre Licking County, Ohio campus planned for eight AI-ready data centres and up to 800 MW

Cologix is AEP Ohio's customer for onsite fuel-cell power under a 15-year agreement approved by the PUCO in May 2025; AEP Ohio buys, owns and operates the Bloom Energy fuel cells and Cologix pays for the service

Digital Edge: about USD 640m of new equity and USD 1bn of debt in January 2025; a USD 880m green loan for a 100 MW Chonburi campus in a joint venture with B.Grimm Power (May 2026); Stonepeak's credit arm was a mandated lead arranger of its USD 575m holding-company loan (May 2026); John Freeman succeeded founder Samuel Lee as chief executive from Q2 2025

Montera's leadership — a founder-CEO from Yondr and Google, a CTO and a Chief Delivery Officer — is the team that signs for its equipment; it pledged in August 2026 to comply with the Texas governor's data-centre standards without naming a Texas site
productsAndServices.positioning: Three distinct models under one owner: interconnection-dense metro data centres (Cologix), a pan-Asian developer (Digital Edge) and a greenfield hyperscale builder (Montera).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Controlling equity through flagship funds, a Cologix continuation vehicle and platform-level capital raises with co-investors.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Montera PHX1 in service Q2 2028; Cologix COL5 in Columbus ready for service in Q3 2026; Digital Edge's Mumbai BOM3 under construction.

productsAndServices.name: Minority and preferred positions in data centres — CoreSite, Princeton Digital Group, Carrier Colo
productsAndServices.description: Stonepeak also holds data-centre positions it does not control. American Tower's FY2025 10-K says Stonepeak holds about 29% of the common equity of American Tower's US data-centre business (CoreSite) and all of its mandatorily convertible preferred equity, about 36% on a fully converted basis, with American Tower keeping control. Princeton Digital Group, an Asian operator, took a USD 1.3bn preferred-equity commitment from Stonepeak in July 2025, with Warburg Pincus remaining its largest shareholder. In November 2025 Stonepeak and Columbia Capital agreed to buy IPB Internet Provider in Berlin, operator of the Carrier Colo data centres.
highlights: A development partnership with American Tower to build a Denver data centre gives Stonepeak the controlling interest and American Tower a minority (AMT 10-K)
None of these positions gives Stonepeak control of equipment buying; the operator's management signs
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Minority common equity, mandatorily convertible preferred and preferred-equity commitments.

productsAndServices.name: Energy and energy transition — Kingdom, CVOW, Louisiana LNG, solar and distributed energy
productsAndServices.category: Private markets — power, storage and LNG
productsAndServices.description: Stonepeak's energy book mixes one controlled storage platform with large non-controlling stakes. Kingdom, a battery-storage platform 'established by Stonepeak' and headquartered in Singapore, owns nine Japanese projects totalling 479 MW that each hold a 20-year capacity-market contract; it closed its first project financing, for the 29 MW Mimasaka project with CATL batteries, with MUFG in April 2026. Stonepeak bought a 50% noncontrolling interest in Dominion Energy's 2.6 GW Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project in October 2024, paying USD 2.6bn at closing, and a 40% interest in Woodside's Louisiana LNG infrastructure company in June 2025. It holds minority stakes in two Repsol US solar portfolios and announced an equity investment in AMPYR Distributed Energy, a UK and European onsite-solar platform, on 22 September 2026.
highlights: Kingdom descends from the platform Stonepeak formed with Singapore's CHC in May 2024: the four projects it won in Japan's first long-term decarbonisation auction (131 MW) and the five awarded in April 2025 (348 MW) sum to its 479 MW; the same chief executive leads it

Other controlled or Stonepeak-created power platforms: TerraWind Renewables (80%, with Shizen Energy 20%; Asian onshore wind, March 2024) and WahajPeak (Middle East solar, wind and storage, launched August 2025); Stonepeak's renewables and energy-transition platforms totalled '10.4 GW of renewable energy in operations, under construction, or in development' in August 2025

CVOW: Virginia Power 'will retain full operational control of the construction and operations', and Stonepeak holds 'customary minority interest rights'; Stonepeak funds 50% of costs up to USD 11.3bn and has an option to share costs above that (Dominion 8-K, February 2024)

Louisiana LNG: Stonepeak committed USD 5.7bn toward the foundation development's capital expenditure and paid about USD 1.9bn at completion; Woodside operates and Bechtel is the lump-sum EPC contractor (Woodside, June 2025)
Repsol: 46.3% of a 777 MW operating solar-and-storage portfolio for USD 340m (closed July 2025) and 43.8% of the 629 MW Outpost solar project for USD 252.5m (December 2025)

AMPYR Distributed Energy: the transaction was 'expected to close in the coming days'; stake and price undisclosed; its parent AGP Sustainable Real Assets took a strategic preferred investment from Stonepeak in 2023
Ørsted: a stake in four US onshore wind farms (957 MW) for about USD 300m in March 2024, with Stonepeak receiving 80% of cash distributions and Ørsted remaining managing member
productsAndServices.positioning: Stonepeak controls the storage developer it created (Kingdom) and finances the rest as a co-owner beside an operator — Dominion, Woodside, Repsol, AGP.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Platform equity (Kingdom), joint-venture and noncontrolling interests (CVOW, Louisiana LNG, Repsol) and growth equity (AMPYR Distributed Energy).
productsAndServices.roadmap: CVOW's final turbines are expected by the end of 2027 (Dominion Q2 2026 10-Q); Kingdom targets further project financings; the AMPYR Distributed Energy closing was pending at 5 October 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Signed acquisitions — Cleco, Castrol and Allgas
productsAndServices.category: Private markets — utilities and industrial platforms
productsAndServices.description: Three signed deals would add controlled businesses on closing. With Bernhard Capital Partners, Stonepeak agreed on 27 April 2026 to buy Cleco Group, a Louisiana regulated electric utility serving about 298,000 customers, from a consortium of Macquarie Asset Management, BCI and Manulife; 'upon close, Stonepeak will hold the majority interest', subject to customary regulatory approvals; Cleco would remain regulated by the Louisiana Public Service Commission. On 24 December 2025 Stonepeak agreed to acquire a majority controlling interest in Castrol from bp at an enterprise value of about USD 10.1bn, with bp keeping 35% and CPP Investments investing up to USD 1.05bn for an indirect stake. In December 2025 it agreed to buy Allgas, a Queensland gas distributor.
highlights: Cleco Power owns generating units with a rated capacity of 2,676 MW; Cleco would remain locally managed and regulated in Louisiana (Stonepeak release)
Castrol's USD 10.1bn is an enterprise value for the whole business, not Stonepeak's equity cheque
Closing of none of the three is on the record as of 5 October 2026
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Majority equity alongside co-investors (Bernhard Capital at Cleco; bp and CPP Investments at Castrol).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Cleco awaits regulatory approvals; Castrol and Allgas closings not announced.

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **Stonepeak is a directory of buyers, not a door**: Stonepeak Partners LP places no equipment orders, and the purchase orders come from Cologix, Digital Edge, Montera and Kingdom, each through its own management. Basis: the platforms' own releases and Stonepeak's release language on each; Kingdom's April 2026 financing release is the only one naming a supplier (CATL). A seller reaches these buyers through Stonepeak's portfolio and sells to the platform.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **on its largest power positions Stonepeak is a financier beside an operator**. Basis: Dominion's 8-K says Virginia Power 'will retain full operational control of the construction and operations' of CVOW; Woodside operates Louisiana LNG with Bechtel as contractor; Repsol and Ørsted keep control of the US renewables Stonepeak co-owns. CVOW's estimated cost has risen to about USD 11.7bn (Dominion's Q2 2026 10-Q), above the USD 11.3bn ceiling on Stonepeak's mandatory contributions; above that ceiling Stonepeak's further contributions are optional, and Virginia Power funds 67–83% of any it chooses to share (Dominion 8-K, February 2024).

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Stonepeak's distinctive method is platform creation, which makes its buyers young and management-led**. Basis: Digital Edge, Kingdom, Montera, TerraWind and WahajPeak were each formed around a team with a Stonepeak capital commitment. For a seller that means the procurement relationship is with founders and delivery chiefs recruited from hyperscalers and integrators, and the first purchase orders arrive as each platform's first project is financed — as Kingdom's did in April 2026.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Cleco would turn Stonepeak from a utility co-owner into a utility owner**. Basis: the April 2026 agreement gives Stonepeak the majority of a Louisiana utility with 2,676 MW of generation on closing. Until approvals arrive Cleco is a pending buyer, and its procurement would remain with its local management under the Louisiana Public Service Commission.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **Stonepeak's fundraising is slower at the flagship than its growth suggests**. Basis: Fund V had sold USD 7.29bn by January 2025 (Form D) against a USD 15bn target reported by Infrastructure Investor and has no close on the record; Dorrell cut his own Fund I carry in February 2026. Against that, the firm's published AUM rose from USD 61.1bn (March 2024) to about USD 93bn (March 2026), carried by strategy funds, Cologix's continuation vehicle and the wealth channel.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Cleco approvals:* a closing would make Stonepeak the majority owner of a regulated utility. *AMPYR Distributed Energy closing notice:* the stake size would show whether Stonepeak controls it. *Kingdom's next project financings:* each names its battery supplier. *Montera PHX1 (in service Q2 2028):* the first Montera campus and its equipment choices. *Fund V final close:* the size the flagship reached. *CVOW completion, expected by end-2027:* whether costs stay near USD 11.7bn.

relationships.scale: 50% noncontrolling interest; USD 2.6bn paid to Dominion at closing
relationships.via: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind Commercial Project (2.6 GW)
relationships.note: Stonepeak owns a 50% noncontrolling interest in CVOW through OSW Project LLC; Dominion's Virginia Power keeps full operational control of construction and operations.
relationships.context:
Dominion's 8-K of 26 February 2024 records the equity capital contribution agreement with Dunedin Member LLC, a Stonepeak vehicle: Stonepeak paid 50% of construction costs incurred to closing (less a USD 145m withholding), funds 50% of remaining costs up to a total of USD 11.3bn, and may share costs between USD 11.3bn and USD 13.7bn, with Virginia Power then contributing 67–83%; Virginia Power 'will retain full operational control', and Stonepeak has 'customary minority interest rights'. The sale closed in October 2024, with Virginia Power receiving USD 2.6bn.

Dominion's Q2 2026 10-Q puts the estimated cost at about USD 11.7bn, with the final turbines expected by the end of 2027, and lists Stonepeak's optional contributions among its risks. Dominion builds and operates the project and signs its equipment contracts.

relationships.scale: Third-party owners receive less than 17% of fee income and carried interest
relationships.via: Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital (formerly Dyal)
relationships.note: Blue Owl's GP Strategic Capital funds have held a passive minority interest in Stonepeak's holding company since June 2023, with no control.
relationships.context: Stonepeak's July 2023 release announced a minority investment from Blue Owl's GP Strategic Capital platform. Its Form ADV (April 2026) records that Blue Owl-managed vehicles acquired a minority interest in Stonepeak Partners Holdings LP in June 2023 and made follow-on investments; Blue Owl and other third-party strategic investors together receive less than 17% of the adviser's fee income and of its carried interest, and none has 'control over the day-to-day operations or investment decisions'. Michael Dorrell controls the adviser through its general partner.

relationships.scale: About 98 MW across the AWS and Cologix contracts; Cologix's runs 15 years
relationships.via: AEP Ohio onsite fuel-cell electricity service
relationships.note: AEP Ohio provides onsite fuel-cell electricity to Cologix, Stonepeak's controlled data-centre platform, under a 15-year PUCO-approved contract; AEP Ohio owns the Bloom Energy fuel cells.
relationships.context:
AEP's release of 5 June 2025 says the PUCO approved AEP Ohio's onsite fuel-cell projects for Amazon Web Services and Cologix and that 'AWS and Cologix will cover the full project costs'; AEP's Q2 2025 10-Q records two contracts totalling about 98 MW under its Bloom Energy fuel-cell purchase agreement. AEP Ohio buys, owns and operates the fuel cells; Cologix is the customer for the electricity.

Stonepeak has controlled Cologix since 2017 and recapitalised it at a USD 3.0bn equity value in 2022.

relationships.via: BESS for the Mimasaka project, Okayama
relationships.note: CATL supplies the batteries for Kingdom's 29 MW Mimasaka project, the first project-financed asset of Stonepeak's Japanese battery-storage platform.
relationships.context: Kingdom's release of April 2026 describes 'a battery energy storage system ("BESS") platform established by Stonepeak' that signed its first long-term project-finance loan with MUFG Bank for the Mimasaka project, a 29 MW battery in Okayama Prefecture, which 'incorporates batteries from CATL'. Kingdom owns nine Japanese projects totalling 479 MW, each with a 20-year capacity-market contract. Kingdom's management signs the supply contract; Stonepeak is the sponsor.

relationships.scale: CPP up to USD 1.05bn, for an indirect stake
relationships.note: CPP Investments agreed to invest up to USD 1.05bn alongside Stonepeak's acquisition of a majority controlling interest in Castrol, taking an indirect stake.
relationships.context: Stonepeak's release of 24 December 2025: Stonepeak agreed to acquire a majority controlling interest in Castrol from bp at an enterprise value of about USD 10.1bn, bp keeping 35%; 'in connection with the transaction, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board ("CPP Investments") will invest up to USD$1.05 billion in support of the transaction, resulting in an indirect stake in Castrol'. No closing is on the record as of 5 October 2026.

relationships.note: Macquarie Asset Management is part of the consortium selling Cleco, the Louisiana utility, to Stonepeak and Bernhard Capital Partners.
relationships.context: Stonepeak's release of 27 April 2026 announces an agreement with Bernhard Capital Partners to acquire Cleco Group from a consortium of Macquarie Asset Management, BCI and Manulife Investment Management, which owned it for about a decade; Stonepeak is to hold the majority interest on closing, subject to customary regulatory approvals.

Its Form ADV is the primary public record of its ownership, regulatory AUM (USD 81.9bn) and private funds (121).

technicalSpecs.notes: An investor passes the buying-authority test only through a platform it controls.
